text: For the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system with a smoothed bore in u and a KdV soliton in v at x=-8, what happens when the soliton encounters the bore at T=8: does the soliton transmit, reflect, fuse, or get destroyed? Can a numerical method (Fourier pseudospectral) keep v_max>=0.5 and u bounded throughout?

ic: u0=1.5*(1-tanh(x/0.5))/2 (bore, u_L=1.5, u_R=0 at x=0), v0=1.5*sech^2(x+8) (soliton at x=-8, amplitude 1.5)
method: Fourier pseudospectral Nx=256 L=30, 2/3-rule dealiasing on ALL terms (linear+nonlinear), classical RK4, dt=2e-4, no additional u-dissipation
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 depth=3 confirms Fourier+2/3+RK4 at dt=2e-4 is stable for this PDE class at amp<=3 up to T=10; BKdV-S1 CLOSED entry rules out no-dealiasing; CLOSED central-FD entries rule out FD for hyperbolic terms. NOT adding u-viscosity yet per progressive-complexity: BKdV-S6 warns this will produce bore Gibbs (u_max~3.4, TV~126 at T=6) but v_max was 0.58>0.5 — run baseline first to observe actual failure mode at T=8 with soliton at x=-8.

rationale: u_max=10.26 >> threshold 5 (FAILS); bore developed extreme Gibbs oscillations exactly as predicted by BKdV-S6. v_max=0.677 passes the >=0.5 threshold but bore is physically meaningless. Mass is exactly conserved. Confirms BKdV-S6 prediction: bore Gibbs with no dissipation.

Single-component upgrade: add explicit linear viscosity nu=5e-2 on u-equation (u_xx term) as directly recommended by BKdV-S6 depth=3 synthesis. Keep all other components identical. BKdV-S6 shows nu>=1e-2 yields u_max_final<=1.62, TV(u)<=27 for this exact bore IC.

method: Fourier pseudospectral Nx=256 L=30, 2/3-rule dealiasing, classical RK4, dt=2e-4, PLUS linear u-viscosity nu=5e-2 on u-equation (nu*u_xx = IFFT(-nu*k^2*u_hat), explicit in RK4)
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S6 depth=3 synthesis directly recommends nu_linear=5e-2 as default for bore-like u ICs; the bank shows nu>=1e-2 yields u_max_final<=1.62 and TV<=27 vs catastrophic TV=126 with no dissipation. Bank rejects nu=1e-4 (ineffective, 7% reduction only) and nu=1e-3 (insufficient). Single-component upgrade over E1: only added the u_xx viscosity term.

rationale: ALL criteria met: (1) final v has a single clean peak at x=10.78 with amplitude 0.5055>=0.5 (soliton survived, transmitted through bore); (2) u_max_final=1.398<5, u_min_final=0.200>0 (bore bounded and positive); (3) bore not blown up: TV_u_final=6.5 (excellent), no negative u at final time. Soliton amplitude dropped from 1.5 to 0.51 after passing through bore — interaction is transmissive/refractive. Physical scenario: soliton at x=-8 moved right at effective speed ~3-4.5 (enhanced by u coupling), interacted with bore centered at x=0 around t~2-4, then emerged as a weaker soliton at x~10.78 by T=8.
E2 satisfies all phenomenon targets: v_max=0.5055>=0.5, u_max=1.398<5, bore clean TV=6.5. Stop early — no further iterations needed.
